entities.summary: Andreas Osiander was a German Lutheran theologian and Protestant reformer who played a crucial role in shaping the Protestant Reformation in Western Europe. Born in unknown circumstances, Osiander was a key figure in the theological disputes that led to the Augsburg Confession in 1530. His work, particularly his 1540 translation of the Bible into German, helped to spread Luther's teachings and contributed to the growth of the Protestant movement. Osiander's influence can be seen in the development of Lutheran theology and the subsequent Protestant-Catholic divisions. He died on November 6, 1552, leaving behind a legacy of theological innovation and controversy. The exact circumstances of his birth remain unknown, adding to the enigma surrounding this pivotal figure in European history.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Andreas Osiander was a key figure in the Protestant Reformation, shaping the development of Lutheran theology and contributing to the growth of Protestantism in Western Europe. His work had a significant impact on the divisions between Protestants and Catholics, which continue to have an impact on Western society today.
